sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014 (CLDF release 2024). lexibank/gravinachadic v1.0: CLDF dataset derived from Gravina's 'Proto-Central Chadic' (2014). Zenodo record 13254095. Mbazla [bald1241]: 88 forms, Source = Seignobos & Tourneux 1984; Tourneux 1987. (Full data also at centralchadic.webonary.org.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wordlist-only data: 80 of 88 Mbazla forms carry tone diacritics copied from the primary notes, three marks in use (acute e.g. sháʼ 'animal', grave+acute trògóʼ 'elephant', macron wāʼ 'breast', rising ǎmbūs 'blood'), which shows Seignobos & Tourneux transcribed (at least) H, L and M pitch levels; no statement about tone or stress anywhere in the dataset.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The phonology of Proto-Central Chadic: the reconstruction of the phonology and lexicon of Proto-Central Chadic, and the linguistic history of the Central Chadic languages. Utrecht: LOT (LOT 375). Baldemu treated as 'Mbazla [bdn]', sec. 3.3.10 (p. 55-56) and sec. 5.3.4 (pp. 113-115).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing about Mbazla/Baldemu stress; the reconstruction explicitly excludes tone and stress. States (p. 113): 'No published phonology exists for any of these languages [Maroua group].. For Mbazla, the data amounts to a total of 390 entries from various sources of differing quality.' Notes word-final *n→ŋ in Mbazla and back-rounding vowel harmony largely attributable to labialized velars.

sources.citation: Brye, Edward. 2003. A rapid appraisal language survey of the Baldemu language (Diamare Division, Far North Province). SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2003-015. Dallas: SIL International. 13 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic rapid appraisal (fieldwork 15 Feb 2000; three elderly speakers located). Appendix B (pp. 7-12) is a 126-item ALCAM word list elicited by Domché-Teko with tone diacritics (acute/grave/macron, e.g. àráy 'eye', ŋgùzó' 'hair', kítīŋ 'nose') on every form; no phonology section, no mention of stress or accent. downloaded from the Internet Archive copy of the SIL file (live SIL host returns not reachable by automated download).

sources.citation: Seignobos, Christian & Henry Tourneux. 2002. Le Nord-Cameroun à travers ses mots: Dictionnaire de termes anciens et modernes, Province de l'Extrême-Nord. Paris: Karthala (Dictionnaires et Langues). 334 p. (entries 'baldamou' p. 28 and 'mbazla' p. 188).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Regional glossary by the two describers of the language. The only linguistic content on Baldemu is the etymology of the ethnonym with one segmental remark (weak prenasalisation of the initial, voiced lateral fricative [zl] rendered [ld] by Kanuri and Fulbe, Kanuri suffix -bu dissimilated to -mu); the form [mbazla] is cited without tone marks here. Nothing on tone, stress or accent; the rest of the 332-page PDF has no other passage on the language (a full-text search for stress/accent baldam/mbazla/balda).

sources.citation: Barreteau, Daniel & Michel Dieu. 2000. Linguistique. In Christian Seignobos & Olivier Iyébi-Mandjek (eds.), Atlas de la province Extrême-Nord Cameroun, planche 3 (with lexicostatistic tables for 58 Chadic languages). Paris: IRD Éditions / MINREST.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology content for mbazla: an identification paragraph ('[34] mbazla : la langue mbazla a été signalée sous le nom de « balda ».. identifiée comme « baldamu » par SEIGNOBOS et TOURNEUX (1984).. Ses derniers locuteurs connus habitent aujourd'hui à Guirvidig'), a row in the lexicostatistic similarity matrix, and four tone-marked example items (oeuf, nuit, deux, main: '34. mbazla 1 aslay 1 avu 1 cáw 6 haŋ'). Tone diacritics on forms only; no statement on tone or stress.
